title: Motion in a Straight Line (1D Kinematics)
subtitle: Zero-to-JEE-Advanced Visual Textbook: Frame of Reference, Calculus Kinematics, Equations of Motion, Gravity Free-Fall, Motion Graphs & 1D Relative Velocity
introduction:
💡 First-Time Reader Intuition: What Is Kinematics?

Mechanics is the branch of Physics that studies how objects move. It is divided into two parts:

  • 1. Kinematics (The “How” of Motion): Describes how things move using position, velocity, acceleration, and time—without worrying about what force caused the motion.
  • 2. Dynamics (The “Why” of Motion): Connects motion to its cause (forces and Newton's Laws).
Is Anything Truly at Rest? (Frame of Reference):
Imagine sitting still inside a moving train. To a passenger next to you, you are at rest. To a person on the station platform, you are moving at 80 km/h! Rest and motion are never absolute; they depend entirely on the observer's chosen coordinate axes and clock.

topics.title: Position, Distance vs. Displacement & Average Speed vs. Average Velocity
topics.theoryHtml:
1.1 Distance (Path Length) vs. Displacement
FeatureDistance ($d$)Displacement ($\Delta x$)
NatureScalar (Magnitude only).Vector (Magnitude & Direction).
SignAlways positive ($>0$).Can be positive, negative, or zero.
PathDepends on actual path taken.Depends ONLY on endpoints $(x_i, x_f)$.
$$\textbf{Universal Inequality:} \quad \boxed{\text{Distance } (d) \ge |\text{Displacement } (\Delta x)|}$$
1.2 Average Speed vs. Average Velocity
$$\boxed{v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{\text{Total Distance}}{\text{Total Time}}} \qquad \bigg| \qquad \boxed{\vec{v}_{\text{avg}} = \frac{\Delta x}{\Delta t}}$$

Two Special Cases for Average Speed:

  • Equal Times ($t$): $v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{v_1 + v_2}{2}$
  • Equal Distances ($d$): $v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}$ (Harmonic Mean)
topics.derivationHtml:
Proof: Equal-Distance Average Speed

Total Time $= \frac{d}{v_1} + \frac{d}{v_2} = d\left(\frac{v_1 + v_2}{v_1 v_2}\right)$. Total Distance $= 2d$.
$$v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{2d}{d\left(\frac{v_1+v_2}{v_1 v_2}\right)} = \frac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}$$

topics.jeeTraps: • Trap: When average velocity is zero on a round trip, average speed is NOT zero!

topics.title: Instantaneous Velocity & Acceleration via Calculus, Turning Points & Reversal of Motion
topics.theoryHtml:
2.1 Calculus Definitions
$$\boxed{v(t) = \frac{dx}{dt}} \qquad \bigg| \qquad \boxed{a(t) = \frac{dv}{dt} = v\frac{dv}{dx}}$$
topics.derivationHtml:
Calculus Relations

$\Delta x = \int v\,dt$, $\quad d = \int |v|\,dt$, $\quad \frac{v^2 - u^2}{2} = \int a\,dx$.
topics.graphSvg: <svg viewBox='0 0 680 180' style='width:100%;max-width:680px;height:auto;'><rect width='680' height='180' rx='8' fill='#080b12' stroke='#1e293b'/><text x='340' y='95' fill='#00e676' font-size='13' font-weight='bold' text-anchor='middle'>v = dx/dt  |  a = dv/dt = v dv/dx</text></svg>
topics.jeeTraps: • Trap: Zero velocity at maximum height does not mean zero acceleration! Acceleration is still $-g$.

topics.title: Uniformly Accelerated Motion: The 4 Kinematic Equations & Galileo's Law
topics.theoryHtml:
3.1 The 4 Kinematic Equations ($a = \text{const}$)
$$v = u + at, \quad s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2, \quad v^2 = u^2 + 2as, \quad S_n = u + \frac{a}{2}(2n-1)$$
topics.derivationHtml:
Derivation of v = u + at

$\int_u^v dv = a \int_0^t dt \implies v - u = at$.
topics.graphSvg: <svg viewBox='0 0 680 180' style='width:100%;max-width:680px;height:auto;'><rect width='680' height='180' rx='8' fill='#080b12' stroke='#1e293b'/><text x='340' y='95' fill='#ffab00' font-size='13' font-weight='bold' text-anchor='middle'>Galileo Odd Numbers: S_n ∝ (2n − 1)</text></svg>
topics.jeeTraps: • Trap: $S_n$ gives net displacement during the $n^{\text{th}}$ second, not total distance if motion reverses.

topics.title: Motion Under Gravity: Free Fall, Vertical Projection Symmetry & Tower Projections
topics.theoryHtml:
4.1 Vertical Projectile Symmetry
$$T = \frac{2u}{g}, \quad H_{\max} = \frac{u^2}{2g}, \quad t_1 + t_2 = T, \quad h = \frac{1}{2}g t_1 t_2, \quad t_0 = \sqrt{t_1 t_2}$$
topics.derivationHtml:
Tower Formula Proof

$-H = ut - \frac{1}{2}gt^2 \implies \frac{1}{2}gt^2 - ut - H = 0 \implies t_0 = \sqrt{t_1 t_2}$.
topics.graphSvg: <svg viewBox='0 0 680 180' style='width:100%;max-width:680px;height:auto;'><rect width='680' height='180' rx='8' fill='#080b12' stroke='#1e293b'/><text x='340' y='95' fill='#00f0ff' font-size='13' font-weight='bold' text-anchor='middle'>Free Fall: a = −g always</text></svg>
topics.jeeTraps: • Trap: Object dropped from a rising balloon inherits the balloon's upward velocity.

topics.title: Motion Graphs Analysis (x-t, v-t, a-t & v-x)
topics.theoryHtml:
5.1 Slope & Area Summary
$$\text{x-t slope} = v, \quad \text{v-t slope} = a, \quad \text{v-t area} = \Delta x, \quad \text{a-t area} = \Delta v$$
topics.graphSvg: <svg viewBox='0 0 680 180' style='width:100%;max-width:680px;height:auto;'><rect width='680' height='180' rx='8' fill='#080b12' stroke='#1e293b'/><text x='340' y='95' fill='#00e676' font-size='13' font-weight='bold' text-anchor='middle'>v-t Area = Displacement</text></svg>
topics.jeeTraps: • Trap: Area under $a$-$t$ graph gives $\Delta v$, not final velocity $v_f$.

topics.title: 1D Relative Motion: Chasing, Overtaking & Elevator Frames
topics.theoryHtml:
6.1 Relative Velocity
$$v_{AB} = v_A - v_B, \quad a_{AB} = a_A - a_B, \quad g_{\text{eff}} = g \pm a_0$$
topics.graphSvg: <svg viewBox='0 0 680 180' style='width:100%;max-width:680px;height:auto;'><rect width='680' height='180' rx='8' fill='#080b12' stroke='#1e293b'/><text x='340' y='95' fill='#ff0055' font-size='13' font-weight='bold' text-anchor='middle'>Elevator Frame: g_eff = g ± a₀</text></svg>
topics.jeeTraps: • Trap: Two falling bodies have relative acceleration $a_{AB} = 0$.

questions.prompt: A cyclist travels the first third of a straight road at $10\text{ km/h}$, the second third at $20\text{ km/h}$, and the final third at $60\text{ km/h}$. Find the average speed.
questions.explanation: Harmonic mean for 3 equal distances gives $18\text{ km/h}$.
